AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To keep off rain and sun
   B. To hide it from animals only
   C. To stop it from rotting
   D. To make it heavier

2. After about how long should the compost heap first be turned? (1 mark)
   A. One hour
   B. Never
   C. One year
   D. Two to three weeks

3. What is soil erosion? (1 mark)
   A. Adding manure to soil
   B. Planting trees
   C. Watering the garden
   D. The washing or blowing away of top soil

4. What is compost manure? (1 mark)
   A. Fertiliser made in a factory
   B. A kind of animal feed
   C. A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   D. Fresh soil from a river bank

5. Which of these crops can be watered with drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Only crops under water
   B. Tomatoes in rows
   C. Nothing at all
   D. Only trees in forests

6. Which pupil is saving water? (1 mark)
   A. One who pours buckets over the whole bed
   B. One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   C. One who waters at midday
   D. One who leaves the tap running

7. Where should the holes in the pipe be placed? (1 mark)
   A. Only near the bucket
   B. Only at the end of the row
   C. Far away from the plants
   D. Next to each plant

8. Why is the water container placed on a stand? (1 mark)
   A. So it looks tall
   B. To hide it from birds
   C. To keep it out of the sun forever
   D. So water flows down through the pipe

9. How is charcoal made? (1 mark)
   A. By burning wood slowly with little air
   B. By boiling water
   C. By mixing soil and water
   D. By drying maize

10. Which stove saves more charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. An open fire in the wind
   B. An improved jiko
   C. A broken pot
   D. A stone on the ground

11. Why does a lid on a pot save fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the pot lighter
   B. It stops the food from cooking
   C. It cools the food
   D. It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster

12. Which statement about a three-stone fire is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It loses a lot of heat to the air
   B. It never needs firewood
   C. It saves the most fuel
   D. It is completely smoke-free

13. What is poaching? (1 mark)
   A. Feeding wild animals
   B. Planting trees
   C. Watering crops
   D. Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals

14. How do bees and butterflies help crops and fruit trees? (1 mark)
   A. They eat the fruit
   B. They carry pollen from flower to flower
   C. They water the plants
   D. They dig the soil

15. Why should a scarecrow be moved every few days? (1 mark)
   A. It grows
   B. The pole is too heavy
   C. It gets too hot
   D. Animals get used to one that never moves

16. Which of these makes a scarecrow shine in the sun? (1 mark)
   A. Old CDs or shiny strips
   B. Soil
   C. Wet leaves
   D. Mud

17. Why do we label the seedbed rows? (1 mark)
   A. To give plants names
   B. To decorate
   C. To scare birds
   D. To remember the crop and the date sown

18. About how far apart should carrot plants be after thinning? (1 mark)
   A. About 5 cm
   B. Touching each other
   C. 5 metres
   D. About 1 mm

19. How deep should tiny seeds be sown? (1 mark)
   A. On top of a heap
   B. About 30 cm
   C. As deep as a hand
   D. About 1 cm

20. What is direct sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   B. Watering seeds
   C. Buying young plants
   D. Sowing in a nursery

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to make a scarecrow. (4 marks)

22. Compare a watering can with drip irrigation. (4 marks)

23. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

24. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)

25. Give three peaceful ways of protecting crops from birds and animals apart from a scarecrow. (3 marks)

26. Name three safety rules when using gas for cooking. (3 marks)

27. Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months. (4 marks)

28. Give three ways of saving fuel when cooking. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

2. D — Two to three weeks
   Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

3. D — The washing or blowing away of top soil
   Bare soil can be carried away by rain or wind.

4. C — A dark crumbly material made when plant and animal wastes rot
   Compost is organic manure made from rotted wastes.

5. B — Tomatoes in rows
   Drip systems suit row crops such as tomatoes and kale.

6. B — One who waters with a drip bottle beside each plant
   Drip watering is the most water-saving.

7. D — Next to each plant
   Water must fall near the roots.

8. D — So water flows down through the pipe
   A raised container gives water the push to flow down.

9. A — By burning wood slowly with little air
   Charcoal is wood partly burnt in limited air.

10. B — An improved jiko
   An improved jiko holds heat around the pot.

11. D — It keeps the heat in so food cooks faster
   Less heat escapes so less fuel is used.

12. A — It loses a lot of heat to the air
   Open fires waste heat.

13. D — Illegal killing or capturing of wild animals
   Poaching is against the law.

14. B — They carry pollen from flower to flower
   Pollination helps fruits and seeds to form.

15. D — Animals get used to one that never moves
   Animals learn that something still is harmless.

16. A — Old CDs or shiny strips
   Shiny objects flash and scare animals.

17. D — To remember the crop and the date sown
   Labels prevent confusion.

18. A — About 5 cm
   Carrots need a few centimetres to grow roots.

19. D — About 1 cm
   The smaller the seed, the shallower it should be sown.

20. A — Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   The seedlings are never moved.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Fix a long pole firmly in the ground; tie a shorter stick across it; put a stuffed head on top; dress with a stuffed shirt and hat; add tins or shiny strips.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: A watering can wets a wide area and much water is lost by running off and by evaporation. Drip irrigation puts water beside the roots slowly, so less is used, fewer weeds grow, and the leaves stay dry.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the watering can, 2 marks for drip irrigation.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Nets, fences, noise makers, shiny objects, guarding at the time animals come (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Keep the cylinder upright and away from fire; close the valve after use; if you smell gas open windows and do not light a flame.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a lid on the pot, cut food small, use dry firewood, put out the fire after cooking, soak beans first, or use an improved jiko (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
